text: Patient presents with acute chest pain. EKG shows ST elevation. Diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction (MI). Prescribed aspirin and statins.
Patient is a 45-year-old male. Family history is significant for myocardial infarction in his father at age 50. Patient denies any chest pain or shortness of breath today. Here for routine physical.
Rule out MI. Patient has severe acid reflux which mimics heart attack symptoms, but troponin levels are normal.
History of present illness: 60yo female with known Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Blood sugar is well controlled on Metformin.
Patient's mother had diabetes. Patient's HgbA1c is 5.2, indicating no diabetes at present.
Patient reports experiencing a 'heart attack' in 2010, but medical records from that hospital show it was a panic attack.
Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: Increase lisinopril to 20mg daily.
Patient's blood pressure is 110/70. No signs of hypertension.
Patient is heavily pregnant and experiencing gestational diabetes. Requires close monitoring.
Review of Systems: Cardiovascular: (-) Chest pain. (-) Palpitations. Respiratory: (-) Shortness of breath.
